name: GROUNDLINE: The Shelf Mesh Dispatch
description: A rotating pirate news and tactical information broadcast that airs irregularly on encrypted Shelf mesh nodes, typically in 40-to-90-minute bursts before the signal migrates. GROUNDLINE covers corponation security sweeps, illegal augmentation clinic raids, debt enforcement patterns, and Shelf-level political organizing — interspersed with practical segments on BCI countermeasures, basic wound care for augmentation complications, and how to identify plainclothes contractor surveillance. The broadcast has no fixed host; different voices read each segment, and the editorial collective has never been identified.
cultural_impact: GROUNDLINE's pre-raid alert system — a specific three-tone audio signature pushed to subscribed mesh nodes — has been credited by Shelf community health workers with reducing augmentation clinic casualties during enforcement sweeps by an estimated 30% in covered zones.
story_hooks: A crew is offered a substantial sum to identify GROUNDLINE's editorial collective — by a source that claims to be a concerned family member but whose financial trail leads somewhere much colder.
GROUNDLINE has gone silent for eleven days — no migration signal, no handoff message — and the Shelf communities that depended on its raid warnings are starting to feel it.

One of the arrested individuals who 'didn't talk' is reaching out through a cutout: she did talk, under neural interrogation, and she doesn't know what she gave up — she needs someone to find out before GROUNDLINE does.
